<div class="masthead">
  <div>
    <div class="eyebrow">Professor of Psycholinguistics · University of Oxford</div>
    <h1>Understanding meaning in the mind</h1>
    <p class="lede">I study the cognitive representations that underlie linguistic meaning: how they are structured, constructed from linguistic input and context, accessed in memory, and used in inference.</p>
    <p class="lede" style="font-size:1.05rem; margin-top:.85rem;">My work combines linguistic theory and experimental psycholinguistics because theories of representation and theories of processing constrain one another.</p>

  </div>

<section class="section">
  <div class="section-head">
    <div>
      <div class="section-kicker">Research at a glance</div>
      <h2>Meaning is represented, constructed, inferred and remembered.</h2>
    </div>
    <a href="research/index.html">Explore the research →</a>
  </div>
  <p class="research-intro">I use linguistic theory to formulate precise hypotheses about meaning and experimental psycholinguistics to investigate how those representations are built and used in real time. The same evidence can, in turn, inform the linguistic theory.</p>

  <div class="concept-grid">
    <a class="concept" href="research/index.html#representation" style="text-decoration:none;">
      <div class="concept-num">01</div><h3>Representation</h3>
      <p>What is the format and structure of the representations that underlie linguistic meaning?</p>
      <div class="tag">Explore this work →</div>
    </a>
    <a class="concept" href="research/index.html#construction" style="text-decoration:none;">
      <div class="concept-num">02</div><h3>Construction</h3>
      <p>How are meaningful representations built incrementally from linguistic input, context and knowledge?</p>
      <div class="tag">Explore this work →</div>
    </a>
    <a class="concept" href="research/index.html#inference" style="text-decoration:none;">
      <div class="concept-num">03</div><h3>Inference & expectation</h3>
      <p>How do comprehenders anticipate and infer information that is not explicitly given?</p>
      <div class="tag">Explore this work →</div>
    </a>
    <a class="concept" href="research/index.html#memory" style="text-decoration:none;">
      <div class="concept-num">04</div><h3>Memory & knowledge</h3>
      <p>How do stored knowledge and memory retrieval constrain interpretation, and what representations persist afterwards?</p>
      <div class="tag">Explore this work →</div>
    </a>
  </div>
</section>

<section class="section">
  <div class="split">
    <div>
      <div class="section-kicker">Prospective researchers</div>
      <h2>PhD students and postdocs</h2>
      <p>I am interested in working with researchers who want to investigate the cognitive representation of meaning, particularly where linguistic theory and experimental approaches can inform one another.</p>
      <p>Projects might concern linguistic representation, incremental interpretation, inference and prediction, memory and knowledge, or related questions at the interface of language and cognition.</p>
